title: Black Light FTL Adaptive Spatiotemporal Refinement Registry

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Prevent a short-lived moving saddle, shear fork, covariance bloom, rapidly rotating tidal eigensystem, or rapidly changing gravitational interval from falling between otherwise adequate route samples.

refinementRules: Refine a continuous interval when any configured physical, temporal, covariance, source-motion, acceleration-direction, or tracked tidal-eigenbasis criterion exceeds its tolerance.
Principal tidal eigenvalues remain separate physical quantities; scalar eigenvalue changes and eigenaxis rotations are distinct refinement evidence.
Raw numerical eigenvector ordering is not stable branch identity. Tidal axes must be branch-matched by continuity and sign-aligned before rotation is interpreted.

When eigenvalues become near-degenerate, individual eigenvectors inside the degenerate subspace are not physically unique; refinement should preserve the degeneracy state rather than inventing a large axis rotation.
Encounter-time span is a sampling-control criterion, not a physical hazard score.
Covariance growth is evidence about uncertainty, not a substitute for gravitational severity.
Source motion is normalized by source-to-field-point range only to form a dimensionless refinement trigger; it is not an FTL penalty coefficient.
Adaptive refinement stops at the declared depth or sample ceiling and must report that ceiling if unresolved intervals still request subdivision.
Sampled extrema and finite-difference behavior remain numerical evidence rather than proof that no sharper interior extremum exists.
generatorRules: The refinement runtime consumes the family encounter-time runtime; it does not duplicate source propagation or gravity equations.
The tidal eigenbranch tracker is a downstream physical-geometry authority over the already resolved tidal tensors; it does not create fictional FTL lane topology.
Only CONTINUOUS_PROJECTED_PROGRESS receives intermediate midpoint samples.
PRECOMMIT_ENDPOINT and ANCHORED_PORTAL retain their explicit endpoint/mouth timing semantics and may not gain fabricated corridor samples.

Every inserted midpoint is recomputed through the authoritative encounter-time resolver so source propagation, covariance, model validity, physical environment, and tidal eigensystem can all be evaluated at the new epoch.
A CONFLICT, OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY, UNRESOLVED midpoint, or unresolved degenerate eigenspace remains blocking evidence and may not be replaced by interpolation.
Refinement tolerances are versioned engineering controls rather than constants of nature.
canonSafeguards: This registry does not establish that any FTL method is physically realizable.
Adaptive sampling and tidal eigenbranch tracking improve numerical evidence density; they do not create new race, civilization, manufacturer, or historical canon.
A selected family used for route simulation does not establish that a named civilization uses that family.
Missing source velocity, covariance, epoch, family-boundary state, or model-validity evidence remains missing.
Ordinary gravity, tidal eigenvectors, and covariance may not manufacture an exotic family-boundary hazard or silently set it to zero.
A numerical eigenbasis inside a degenerate eigenspace is not a canonical physical direction.
PRECOMMIT and anchored-portal families may not receive fabricated intermediate ordinary-space encounter epochs.
Hitting a numerical sample ceiling is not evidence that the underlying route is safe or converged.
